mechanism: Conveyor ('horizontal travelling') belt screen: belt runs ALONG the face toward the apex entrance at 0.5-1.0x sweep
how_it_works: Vertically hung endless belt of mesh panels travels horizontally toward the bypass; a bell pinned to the mesh has ~zero velocity relative to the belt, so friction carries it to the apex instead of stalling it. Panels on cassettes; end-turn sprocket just upstream of the apex mouth with a smooth hand-off lip
precedent_and_source: Bates 1970, USFWS Bureau of Commercial Fisheries Fishery Leaflet 633: model V in Stanfield Canal (OR) 1967, juvenile steelhead+coho diversion 97-100%; model VI 85 ft long screened >1,000 cfs (28 m3/s) at 6 ft depth, up to 3 ft/s; text: 'travel of the screen can be matched to the velocity of the water', 'nonswimming forms, such as eggs ... can be collected on the screen and safely carried ... into the bypass'; pressure-release panels swing open. Bates & Vanderwalker: 100% in 37 tests, >11,000 coho (REPORTED). Not commercialised later (no modern vendor found)
expected_effect: Virtual tank (this folder, 4 seeds x 30 bells): eta_r 0.42 -> 1.00 at 0.25-1.2x sweep; 1.00 even with mu 1.0 + 3 Pa adhesion, 3% bypass, 15 deg; v4 layout 0.77 -> 1.00. These are UPPER BOUNDS (2.5-D, the belt reaches the pocket in the model). ESTIMATE at prototype: face guidance 0.95-0.99, limited by end-turn hand-off, 3-D under/over leakage, seal gaps
harm_risks: Low: bells move with the mesh (no shear). Risks: pinch at belt end-turn/side seals (needs <=1.75 mm gaps per NMFS and a smooth lip), turtles riding the belt to the mouth (excluder downstream handles), belt jam -> must fail to a static screen, never to an open hole
cost_complexity: High: ~171 m of belt per lane; it replaces the v4 vertically-cleaned belt bays rather than adding to them (same cassette idea, belt turned 90 deg). Mechanical complexity of a long horizontal chain; segmenting into 3-4 belts each ending at an entrance is easier. ESTIMATE cost +10-30% over v4 belt screens
how_to_test: Tank: drive a mesh loop (bicycle chain + nylon mesh) along the T03 face at 0-1.2x sweep; count bells to bypass, stuck, damaged; film the end-turn hand-off. Virtual: sim/mech_vtank.py (done); add an end-turn gap model

mechanism: Apex entrance sized for most of the load + 4 entrances + 20% entrance flow + flared scoop mouth >= 4-5 bell diameters
how_it_works: Terminal entrance at the downstream apex (NMFS 8.6.2/11.9.1.3 'bypass entrance at the apex and downstream-most point'), mouth flared so bells are not arching; acceleration <=0.2 ft/s per ft
precedent_and_source: NMFS 2022 8.6.2.4-8.6.2.8 (VERIFIED); 03_cfd_flow T3 (100% with apex, 2-D); 07_virtual_tank (4 entr + 20% = 0.73; 35% = 0.82); this folder D0 0.77
expected_effect: Already in v4.1. Baseline 0.73-0.82 (virtual tank). Real Gulf bells are 6.5-12 cm vs 0.46-0.9 m mouths (ratio 4-14) so arching should be rarer than in the tank (4-6 cm bells in a 6 cm mouth) - ESTIMATE
harm_risks: Fast mouth (0.4-0.7 m/s) exceeds juvenile turtle swim speed -> excluder grid required (v4)
cost_complexity: Medium (dewatering stage needed, already in v4)
how_to_test: T03/T04 with mouth width 3-5 bell diameters; F01 flume

mechanism: Second catch screen in series (secondary angled screen across the lane downstream, or the plant's own screens with live return)
how_it_works: Anything that slips past screen 1 meets screen 2 with its own bypass. Combined leak = (1-eta1)(1-eta2) only if failures are independent; same-cause failures (sticky bells, seal gaps) are correlated
precedent_and_source: Duplex principle in 02_hydraulics T03 (duplex curtain 98-99% capture, model); dual screens are common at fish facilities (primary+secondary, NMFS 8.6.2.9)
expected_effect: With eta1 0.95 and eta2 0.6-0.8 (independent): leak 1-2%. With correlation the gain is smaller (ESTIMATE leak 2-4%)
harm_risks: Doubles face exposure time; more head loss; a second set of entrances to keep turtle-safe
cost_complexity: High (second full-width screen per lane) - cheaper as a short partial catch screen near the forebay
how_to_test: Tank: two screens in series, release bells upstream, count leak past each
verdict: CONDITIONAL - add only if pilot eta_r < 0.95

mechanism: Low-adhesion belt/mesh surface: foul-release silicone (PDMS) or hydrophobic coating on polymer mesh; SLIPS only as research
how_it_works: Lowers bell-mesh friction and mucus/nematocyst adhesion so pinned bells slide; also cuts biofouling of the mesh
precedent_and_source: Superhydrophobic/PDMS surfaces inhibited Nemopilema nematocyst adhesion (Materials 2024, PMC11643888, lab); SLIPS antifouling in marine tests but lubricant loss is the main failure (PMC11595577); zwitterionic brushes mu 0.0004-0.05 (lab, not seawater mesh)
expected_effect: Virtual tank: mu 0.4 -> 0.1/0.05 gives 0.42 -> 0.65/0.67 (static face) and v4 0.77 -> 0.85. ESTIMATE +0.05-0.10 on a static screen; ~0 extra with a belt (G1 already removes friction)
harm_risks: Lubricant leaching (SLIPS oils) into a protected site - avoid oils; silicone foul-release is non-biocidal. Coating wear on a moving belt
how_to_test: Tilted wet-mesh slide test with real tissue or gel bells on coated vs bare mesh (T05/T14 add-on)
verdict: ADOPT as cheap backup (silicone foul-release, no oils)

mechanism: Low-velocity wall jets / Coanda sweep along the face (manifold at the upstream edge of each bay)
how_it_works: Thin tangential jets add sweep near the mesh and shake jammed bells loose; pulsed operation unjams the mouth
precedent_and_source: Water-jet arrays were tried as fish deflectors (Bates 1970 fig. 1; 'never completely reliable'); 07 T13: waves 1-4 cm raised eta_r 5-84% by unjamming
expected_effect: Agitation proxy (turbulence 10% -> 25%): 0.42 -> 0.53 (this folder). ESTIMATE +0.05-0.15 on a static face; small with a belt
harm_risks: Jet impact on bells at the nozzle (keep <~1 m/s at the face, ESTIMATE); pumping energy; jets can push bells THROUGH a seal gap if aimed badly
how_to_test: Tank: drip-line manifold along the T03 face, pulsed vs steady; count unjam rate and damage
verdict: OPTIONAL (unjam pulses at the mouth only)

mechanism: Graded porosity baffles behind the downstream 40% + streamlined entrance structures
how_it_works: Evens the through-screen velocity (0.07->0.14 m/s in CFD) so bells are not pinned hard near the apex
precedent_and_source: NMFS 'nearly uniform' flow distribution; 03 T2: uniform k=30 baffle cut >0.12 m/s share 35% -> 18% (graded untested)
expected_effect: Fewer pinned bells near apex; ESTIMATE +0.02-0.05
harm_risks: None significant
how_to_test: CFD graded-baffle run; ADV traverse in flume

mechanism: Surface-skimming apex weir entrance (in addition to the full-depth mouth)
how_it_works: If bells ride the top 1-2 m, a surface weir (>=1-1.5 ft over the crest, NMFS 8.6.2.5) collects them at low flow
precedent_and_source: Catostylus depth: SeaLifeBase 0-1 m is an ecology-based ESTIMATE, not measured; 04 T8 assumed a surface layer; floating surface collectors (Baker River FSC) collect >90% of tagged coho (REPORTED)
expected_effect: Unknown; useful only if pilot sonar shows surface aggregation. ESTIMATE 0 to +0.03
harm_risks: Low
how_to_test: Pilot: ADCP/echosounder + camera depth profile of bells in the lane

mechanism: Light-based attraction/repulsion
how_it_works: Lights at entrances to bias swimming
precedent_and_source: Light responses exist in scyphozoans (Chrysaora mesocosms; Mastigias sun-tracking; Crambionella in captivity) but no Catostylus intake study found; bells cannot out-swim 0.1-0.5 m/s anyway
expected_effect: None claimed
harm_risks: Attracts fish and predators to the mouth; light pollution for turtles at night
how_to_test: Only a lab behaviour assay if ever

mechanism: Closed-loop 'self-learning screen': edge-AI cameras count bells at every entrance and in the leak zone; safe Bayesian optimisation tunes entrance-flow split, belt speed, jet pulses
how_it_works: Counts give a live eta_r estimate; optimiser proposes setpoints inside hard limits (velocity caps, turtle-safe mouth limits); local PLC verifies and applies; interlocks remain hard-wired
precedent_and_source: Jellytoring deep detector F1 95.2% counting jellyfish in video (PMC7146330); DeepMind/Google data-centre cooling: AI proposes, local control verifies, ~30% energy saving, operators supervise (deepmind.google 2018)
expected_effect: ESTIMATE +0.02-0.05 eta_r over fixed setpoints (tracks tide/flow changes); main value is MEASURING eta_r continuously
harm_risks: Wrong counts in turbid water -> bad setpoints; must never override interlocks. Air-gapped on-site edge compute only (FANR-REG-08, IEC 62443)
how_to_test: Tank: webcam + YOLO on T03; scripted optimiser over bypass split; compare with fixed best. Virtual: wrap mech_vtank as the plant
verdict: ADOPT in pilot (advisory first, then bounded auto)

mechanism: Bayesian/generative design optimisation of apex scoop, baffle grading, angle, belt speed on a CFD surrogate
how_it_works: Gaussian-process surrogate over ~6-8 geometry parameters; ~50-100 CFD runs pick the optimum and its uncertainty
precedent_and_source: BO+CFD: Kaplan draft-tube shape (Daniels et al. 2021, Optim. Eng.); KTH: <90 CFD runs for up to 8 parameters (REPORTED)
expected_effect: Design-time only; ESTIMATE +0.01-0.05 over hand-tuned geometry; mostly faster design
harm_risks: Over-fitting a 2-D model; must be checked in tank
how_to_test: Run BO on 03_cfd_flow + particle tracker; verify top 3 in tank

mechanism: Ristroph-type live return at the plant's own screens for the last leakers
how_it_works: Fish buckets on each screen panel, low-pressure spray, separate fish trough, continuous rotation, return away from the intake
precedent_and_source: Arthur Kill 24 h survival 15% unmodified vs 79-92% modified; Indian Point striped bass mortality 53% -> 9% (EPA technology fact sheets, REPORTED); vendor <5% mortality (marketing)
expected_effect: Turns plant-screen deaths of leakers into ~80-90% survival (fish analogue, ESTIMATE). Does not raise eta_r
harm_risks: Gelatinous bells may be torn by spray/buckets; plant modification under FANR
cost_complexity: High (plant modification); the plant screen type not public
how_to_test: Bench: bell on a rotating mesh panel with bucket lip + 0.5-1 bar spray

mechanism: Water-only hydraulic fish lock (2-3 alternating chambers): animals enter at sea level, chamber is filled from below with screened pumped water, animals float up ~6.5 m and exit over a submerged weir into the head tank
how_it_works: Animals never touch a moving part or air; only water is pumped. Carrier water is separated: the lock lifts only a concentrated animal stream; the 2 m3/s pipe flow is made up at the head tank with screened, oxygenated water from ordinary pumps
precedent_and_source: Fish locks/lifts (hopper raised and emptied; locks cycle attract-fill-exit-drain and can run in reverse for downstream passage: Queensland WetlandInfo, REPORTED); NMFS 8.6.3.8 'Fish should ... never be pumped'
expected_effect: Sizing CALC at 0.3/m3: 27 bells/s, 5.2 m3 of bells per 10 min; at <=5% volume fraction ~104 m3 bottom pool per cycle -> 2-3 chambers ~6x6 m, fill ~0.5 m3/s (~50 kW water-only). Survival ESTIMATE 99-99.9%
harm_risks: Crowding in the chamber at bloom peaks (>1/m3 needs more chambers); gate pinch (use slow vertical gates with soft seals, no valves in the animal path); turtle must never enter (excluder upstream)
TRL_for_jellyfish: 3 (concept proven for fish; not for jellyfish)
how_to_test: Tank: 2 m acrylic column filled from below with bells inside; video of contact; T09 damage scoring

mechanism: Rotating-tube Archimedes screw (v4) with mitigations: low rpm, compressible rubber leading edge, D>=3 m, submerged outlet
how_it_works: Blades welded to a rotating tube remove the blade-housing gap (the crush point in Archimedes turbines); leading-edge strike remains
precedent_and_source: USBR Tracy vol. 25: Archimedes lift 98-100% trout survival (VERIFIED in 15); Albert Canal screw TURBINES ~1/3 died, mostly squeezed blade-housing (VERIFIED abstract in 15); 04 contact model
expected_effect: Contact probability CALC with real bells 6.5-12 cm (same model as 04): 0.13-0.24 per screw, i.e. ~25-42% of bells touched over two stages. Survival ESTIMATE 95-99% per stage, 90-98% for two
harm_risks: Blade strike, splashing/air at the top discharge, free fall into the trough
how_to_test: T09 bench: 1:5 rotating-tube screw with gel and real bells, rubber vs steel edge

mechanism: Hidrostal screw-centrifugal pump
how_it_works: Single-vane screw impeller, large free passage
precedent_and_source: Hidrostal: lake trout/whitefish eggs & larvae, juvenile trout >=99% (White et al. 2023 NAJFM 43(3), doi 10.1002/nafm.10901, abstract); Tracy: splittail/Chinook 96 h 93%/96% (REPORTED); delta smelt 87%
expected_effect: ESTIMATE 90-99% for bells (impeller leading edge, high relative velocity); no gelatinous data
harm_risks: Impeller strike; pressurises the line (NMFS prefers gravity)
how_to_test: T09 with a small Hidrostal on loan

mechanism: Vacuum / pressure-vacuum fish pump
how_it_works: Tank evacuated to draw animals, then pressurised
precedent_and_source: Matis/MRI Iceland: vacuum-pumped salmon often injured or dead vs Archimedes ValuePump (industry-linked, REPORTED); Nofima: vacuum alone no internal injury (REPORTED)
expected_effect: Not estimated
harm_risks: Vacuum pulls dissolved gas out -> bubbles under bells (Raskoff et al. 2003: avoid bubbles, VERIFIED in 15); valves pinch
how_to_test: None needed

mechanism: Airlift
how_it_works: Air injection lowers column density
precedent_and_source: Airlifts have no moving parts but survival data for young fish are lacking (Atlantis-Press conference paper, REPORTED)
expected_effect: Not estimated
harm_risks: Bubbles trap under bells -> floating, embolism, damage (Raskoff 2003)
how_to_test: None

mechanism: Low-velocity dewatering: horizontal flat-plate (Farmers-Screen-type) or a short travelling belt dewaterer, smooth perforated plate, no wedge-wire edges facing the flow
how_it_works: Water drains DOWN through a horizontal plate while bells ride over it at >=0.3 m depth; sweep >=20x approach; the surplus 7-16 m3/s returns to the lane
precedent_and_source: NMFS 2022 8.8.4: >=1 ft depth over the downstream end, approach <0.25 ft/s (<0.4 with cleaning), sweep >=2.5 ft/s, better self-cleaning at sweep:approach >20:1 and approach <0.1 ft/s (VERIFIED); USGS: >98% 24 h survival over flat-plate screens, no impingement of coho (REPORTED); NMFS 8.6.2.9 secondary screens meet primary criteria (VERIFIED)
expected_effect: Area CALC for 16 m3/s: 533 m2 at 0.03 m/s, 267 m2 at 0.06 m/s (e.g. 8 m x 35 m). Survival ESTIMATE 99-99.9%
harm_risks: If depth drops, bells strand on the plate (NMFS 8.8 warning) -> level control + auto bypass-open on low level
how_to_test: Tank: perforated tray with tilt-adjustable level, bells swept over at 0.3-0.8 m/s scaled; count stranding/edge damage

mechanism: Live-animal pipe rules: gravity, always >= atmospheric pressure, R/D>=5 bends (R>=8 m at 1.6 m), miters <=15 deg, no valves/hydraulic jumps/free fall, butt-fused smooth HDPE, access ports
how_it_works: Keeps shear, impacts, pressure swings and air out of the animal path
precedent_and_source: NMFS 2022 8.6.3.2-8.6.3.16: smooth joints; 2-12 ft/s (6-12 preferred); no pumps; no free fall; vented/>=atmospheric; R/D>=5; no hydraulic jumps; ports every 150 ft (VERIFIED). Huon 950-1,100 m smolt pipe ~8 min at ~2 m/s with O2 manifolds (REPORTED)
expected_effect: CALC at Q 2 m3/s, ID 1.6 m: v 0.99 m/s (above NMFS 2 ft/s minimum, below 6 ft/s preferred), transit 2.9 h, bulk dissipation ~0.004 W/kg -> Kolmogorov strain ~60 1/s, eddies ~130 um << bell size. Survival ESTIMATE 98-99.8% (no gelatinous data)
harm_risks: 3 h confinement, crowding, stress spawning, fouling inside an idle pipe
how_to_test: Recirculating loop: 3 h at 1 m/s, 1-15 kg/m3, DO logged; score bells at 0/24/96 h

mechanism: Bubble-free oxygenation: dissolve O2 in a screened water-only side-stream (Speece cone / U-tube) and blend at the head tank; trim at in-line points with DO sensors; cap TDG
how_it_works: Animals never meet gas bubbles; DO held near saturation over 3 h
precedent_and_source: Huon O2 manifolds (REPORTED); Speece cone supersaturates outflow 25-50 mg/L (vendor, REPORTED); gas-bubble trauma above ~110% TDG in shallow water (BC guideline, REPORTED); scyphomedusae oxyregulate to <10% air saturation (JEB 2005, REPORTED)
expected_effect: O2 demand CALC (0.05 mL O2/h/g, 0.33 kg bells, 2 m3/s): 0.1/m3 -> 0.32 mg/L per 3 h; 0.3/m3 -> 0.96; 1/m3 -> 3.2 (x2 if stressed -> 6.4 > the 5.56 mg/L saturation at 35.8 C). Injection mandatory above ~0.3/m3
harm_risks: Over-oxygenation / TDG > ~110% at the outlet; dead-animal decay demand; biofilm demand
how_to_test: Loop test above with DO/TDG probes

mechanism: Submerged low-velocity diffuser outlet, no plunge, mid-water depth, >=2 km from reefs
how_it_works: Decelerate to near ambient; release below the wave-mixed layer and above the bed
precedent_and_source: NMFS 8.6.4.2 impact velocity <25 ft/s (7.6 m/s) for fish; outfall in non-eddy, predator-poor area (VERIFIED); 04 T4 reef distances
expected_effect: ESTIMATE design exit <=1 m/s; survival 99.5-100%
harm_risks: Predator aggregation at a fixed outlet; stranding down-drift (twin policy covers)
how_to_test: Pilot: camera at diffuser, drifter tags

mechanism: Turtle excluder grid with round bars at 30-55 deg (TED geometry) so bells slide through without impact
how_it_works: Bells 6.5-12 cm pass ~15 cm clear spacing; inclined bars deflect turtles to the escape chute
precedent_and_source: 50 CFR 223.207 TED bar angle 30-55 deg (VERIFIED in 15)
expected_effect: Survival ESTIMATE 99-99.9% (glancing contact only)
harm_risks: Bells draping over bars at high density
how_to_test: T10/F06 + bell draping count

mechanism: No air anywhere: submerged discharges, vented but flooded transitions, no free fall (NMFS 8.6.3.9), degassing at the head tank before animals arrive
how_it_works: Removes the single most cited gelatinous handling hazard
precedent_and_source: Raskoff et al. 2003 Biol. Bull. 204: avoid air bubbles (VERIFIED in 15)
expected_effect: Prevents a whole failure class (not separately quantified)
harm_risks: None
how_to_test: Visual check in every tank test

mechanism: Fused camera + imaging-sonar turtle/dolphin detector (YOLO-class, edge) as BACKUP to the excluder grid
how_it_works: Two diverse sensors vote; output only raises a hard-wired screw/lock stop request; never the primary barrier
precedent_and_source: Turtle YOLOv7 (drone) P 0.85 / R 0.85; TurtleNet mAP50 0.856; turbid water mAP 0.57 (REPORTED); Bio-YOLOv7 on sonar near nuclear intakes P 0.85 / R 0.83 (REPORTED); 04: required protection >=0.99975, one camera 0.955
expected_effect: Raises system protection only together with the grid (04: 2 cameras + grid ~0.9997). ESTIMATE detection 0.85-0.95 per sensor
harm_risks: False negatives at night/turbid; false stops reduce availability
how_to_test: 300-trial turtle-proxy test, night+turbid; report recall with 95% CI

mechanism: ML surrogate of the drift twin with data assimilation from drifters and intake counts for fast 10-day ensembles
how_it_works: Learned emulator runs thousands of members in seconds; drifter positions update the ensemble
precedent_and_source: DriftNet (deep learning Lagrangian drift, arXiv 2211.09818); Drift Field Net: 7-day error ~60 km, ~20 km better than Mercator (arXiv 2609.16288) (REPORTED)
expected_effect: Faster, larger ensembles; ESTIMATE no change in 1-eta_r, but fewer wrong-outlet releases
harm_risks: Surrogate drift outside training range
how_to_test: Hindcast against the 292 alert windows; pilot drifters

mechanism: Predictive maintenance on belts/drums/lock gates from motor current + dP
how_it_works: Baseline healthy current spectra 2-4 weeks, flag chain wear, mis-tracking, looseness
precedent_and_source: MCSA conveyor mis-tracking/looseness (Sensors 2023, PMC10099345; Huddersfield) (REPORTED)
expected_effect: Keeps belt availability high (04 needs MTBF >=1,000-2,900 h); ESTIMATE fewer unplanned stops
harm_risks: None (advisory)
how_to_test: Seeded-fault bench on a small conveyor

mechanism: Operator copilot for the Bloom Incident OS: alarm rationalisation, drafts procedures for human approval; no safety actions
how_it_works: Runs on-site, air-gapped; reads OS state; suggests, never actuates
precedent_and_source: Argonne PRO-AID generative-AI diagnostics for nuclear operators (2024, REPORTED); KAERI LLM interface on SMR simulator (REPORTED)
expected_effect: Fewer nuisance alarms; faster close-alert response (04: approvals were the late-alert bottleneck). Not quantified
harm_risks: Hallucinated advice -> human approval mandatory; cyber (FANR-REG-08)
how_to_test: Tabletop drills with operators on T6 DES scenarios
